Chapter 15: Rate Limiting and Envoy Filters

Protect your services from overload with rate limiting. Istio supports both local (per-pod) and global (shared across all pods) rate limiting via EnvoyFilter — no code changes needed in Django.

🔴 Advanced ⏱️ ~1.5 hours 🛡️ Protection 🎯 ICA 10%

🎯 What You'll Learn

  • ✅ Implement local rate limiting per pod using EnvoyFilter (token bucket algorithm)
  • ✅ Understand the difference between local (per-pod) and global (Redis-backed) rate limiting
  • ✅ Apply traffic shaping: different limits for regular users vs batch jobs via header matching
  • ✅ Know what HTTP 429 status means and how Retry-After works
  • ✅ Configure EnvoyFilter CRD — the most powerful (and dangerous) Istio resource
  • ✅ Choose between token bucket (burst-friendly) and leaky bucket (constant-rate) algorithms
💡 ICA Exam Tips for Chapter 15
  • "Protect a service from overload" = EnvoyFilter with local rate limiting
  • "Rate limit across all pods" = Global rate limiting (requires Redis + rate limit service)
  • "Rate limit exceeded" = Envoy returns 429 Too Many Requests — Django never sees it
  • "Different limits per user type" = EnvoyFilter with header match (traffic shaping)
  • Local = independent per pod (no Redis), Global = shared counter (Redis). Different use cases!
  • EnvoyFilter CRD: apiVersion networking.istio.io/v1alpha3 — directly patches Envoy config

15.1 Local Rate Limiting (Per-Pod)

Each pod has its own independent rate limit bucket. Pod 1 at limit → Pod 2 still serves normally.

🪣 LOCAL RATE LIMITING — Token Bucket per Pod (100 req/s each)
Pod 1

Token bucket: 100 tok/s
████████░░░ 82/100
✅ Serving normally

Pod 2

Token bucket: 100 tok/s
███████████ 100/100
❌ 429 — AT LIMIT!

Pod 3

Token bucket: 100 tok/s
███░░░░░░░ 30/100
✅ Serving normally

Total capacity: 3 pods × 100 = 300 req/s. Each pod's limit is independent — Pod 2 hitting its limit doesn't affect Pods 1 and 3.

15.2 Global Rate Limiting (Shared Counter)

Rate limit by source IP, user, or API key across ALL pods combined. Requires a Redis-backed rate limit service.

🌐 GLOBAL RATE LIMITING — Architecture
1
Request

IP 203.0.113.42 → jobpost-api

2
Envoy Checks

"Check rate limit for this IP" → gRPC to rate limit service

3
Redis Lookup

IP: 203.0.113.42 count: 987/1000
Under limit ✅

4
Allowed

Request forwarded to Django ✅

1001
Denied

Request #1001: count: 1001/1000
→ 429 Too Many Requests ❌

15.3 Traffic Shaping — Controlling Latency

Apply different rate limits based on request type — protect real users from batch jobs:

👤 Regular User

Header: x-client: browser
No rate limit, full speed
0ms overhead

🤖 Batch Job

Header: x-client: batch-job
EnvoyFilter: 100ms delay
Max 10 req/s

15.X Deep Dive — Token Bucket Algorithm Explained

Envoy's local rate limiter uses the Token Bucket algorithm. Understanding how it works is essential for configuring rate limits correctly on the ICA exam.

🪣 TOKEN BUCKET — Visual Walkthrough (100 req/s, burst 20)
TIME 0s:  Bucket has 20 tokens (maxTokens/burst)
          Request 1 arrives → 1 token consumed → 19 left ✅ 200 OK
          Request 2-20 arrive → tokens consumed → 0 left
          Request 21 arrives → 0 tokens → ❌ 429 Too Many Requests

TIME 1s:  Bucket refills: +10 tokens (tokensPerFill) → 10 tokens
          Now 10 more requests can pass

KEY PARAMETERS:
  maxTokens: 20     = Maximum burst size (bucket capacity)
  tokensPerFill: 10 = Tokens added per fillInterval
  fillInterval: 1s  = How often refill happens
  Effective rate: tokensPerFill / fillInterval = 10 req/s steady
  Burst: Up to maxTokens (20) can pass instantly if bucket is full
💡 ICA Exam: Burst vs Steady Rate

Steady rate: tokensPerFill / fillInterval = 10/s. Burst: maxTokens = 20 can pass at once if bucket is full, then rate drops to 10/s. Set maxTokens to handle traffic spikes without overwhelming the service. For uniform traffic, set maxTokens = tokensPerFill.

🛡️ Rate Limiting — Recap

🪣
Local
Per-pod bucket
🌐
Global
Shared Redis counter
🚦
Shaping
Priority lanes

15.X Deep Dive — Extending Envoy: WebAssembly (Wasm) vs Lua Filters

Istio 1.30 provides two mechanisms to extend Envoy proxy behavior beyond built-in features — WebAssembly (Wasm) plugins and Lua scripts. Both are configured via the TrafficExtension API. This is the replacement for the deprecated Mixer component.

🧩 WASM vs LUA — Extending Envoy Proxies
FeatureWebAssembly (Wasm)Lua Scripts
LanguagesC++, Rust, Go, AssemblyScriptLua only
DistributionOCI registries, HTTP URLs, local filesInlined directly in TrafficExtension YAML
Memory~110-290 MiB (sandbox per plugin)~20-26 MiB (in-process, 10× lower)
IsolationFull VM sandbox — crash containedRuns in-process — crash kills worker thread
Failure policyConfigurable: fail-closed (default) or fail-openFail-open only — no config
SDLCUnit tests, CI/CD, versioned releasesScript lives in the resource — limited tooling
Best forComplex logic, reusable production pluginsSimple transforms, temporary workarounds
🏗️ WebAssembly Architecture
  COMPONENTS:
  • Filter SPI — Proxy-Wasm ABI for building plugins
  • V8 Sandbox Runtime — Embedded in Envoy, runs Wasm modules
  • Host APIs — Access headers, trailers, metadata from within plugin
  • Call-out APIs — Make gRPC/HTTP calls to external services
  • Stats & Logging — Emit metrics and logs from within plugin
  
  LIFECYCLE:
  1. Developer writes plugin in Rust/Go/C++ using Proxy-Wasm SDK
  2. Compile to .wasm binary → push to OCI registry
  3. Create TrafficExtension resource referencing the OCI image
  4. Istio pulls Wasm → distributes to Envoy proxies
  5. Envoy loads Wasm in V8 sandbox → plugin executes per request
📝 TrafficExtension YAML Example — Wasm Plugin
apiVersion: extensions.istio.io/v1alpha1
kind: TrafficExtension
metadata:
  name: custom-header-plugin
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      app: jobpost-api
  phase: AUTHZ  # Execute during authorization phase
  priority: 10
  wasm:
    pluginRef:
      url: oci://registry.io/myorg/custom-header:v1.0.0
      sha256: abc123...
    pluginConfig:
      addHeader: "X-Custom-Header"
      headerValue: "processed-by-wasm"
    failurePolicy: FAIL_CLOSE  # Block traffic if plugin fails
⚠️ ICA Exam: Wasm vs Lua Decision Tree

Use Wasm: Production plugins, complex logic, needs testing/versioning/CI/CD, multiple teams reuse, must NOT crash proxy. Use Lua: Simple header manipulation, one-off transform, temporary fix, minimal memory budget. Neither: Built-in EnvoyFilter suffices for most rate limiting, header manipulation, and routing needs — reach for Wasm/Lua ONLY when EnvoyFilter can't do it.

📝 Chapter 15 — ICA Practice Questions (Hands-On Lab Scenarios)

Q1
Protect jobpost-api from overload with local rate limiting. Task: (a) Write an EnvoyFilter that limits each pod to 100 req/s with burst of 20. (b) Apply to jobpost-api pods via workloadSelector. (c) Test: send 200 req/s to one pod → 100 succeed, 100 get 429. (d) Verify other pods still serve normally (local = per-pod, independent). (e) Explain token bucket: maxTokens=burst, tokensPerFill=refill rate, fillInterval=period.
Show Answer
Answer

EnvoyFilter with applyTo: HTTP_FILTER, SIDECAR_INBOUND. Token bucket: maxTokens (burst), tokensPerFill (refill), fillInterval (period). Each pod has independent bucket — 3 pods × 100 = 300 total. 429 returned on overflow.

Explanation

Local = per-pod, no external dependencies. Global = shared Redis counter. Local is simpler but limits aren't shared across pods.

Q2
Compare local vs global rate limiting. Task: Local: per-pod counter, 3 pods × 100 = 300 req/s independent, no Redis needed. Global: ALL pods share ONE counter, requires Redis-backed rate limit service, total limit applies across entire deployment. Choose local for per-pod protection, global for per-user/per-IP limits. Explain: global = Envoy→gRPC→RateLimitService→Redis (adds latency per request).
Show Answer
Answer

Local: per-Envoy token bucket, independent, no deps. Global: shared Redis counter, gRPC checks per request, Redis required. Global provides Retry-After header; local does not. Choose based on whether limit must span all pods.

Explanation

Local = simple, scales with pods. Global = accurate across all pods, requires Redis infrastructure.

Q3
Test rate limiting behavior. Task: (a) Apply EnvoyFilter with 10 req/s limit. (b) Send 30 rapid requests. (c) Verify: first ~10 succeed (200), rest get 429 Too Many Requests. (d) Verify Django never sees the rejected requests (Envoy blocks at proxy). (e) Explain: 429 returned by Envoy, no application overhead. For global RL, Retry-After header tells clients when to retry.
Show Answer
Answer
for i in $(seq 1 30); do\n  kubectl exec deploy/source -n anihpj -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" http://jobpost-api/health\ndone\n# ~10 × 200, ~20 × 429

Envoy blocks at proxy level — Django never sees rejected requests. 429 = standard rate limit status.

Explanation

429 from Envoy means your request never reached Django. Global RL adds Retry-After header; local does not.

Q4
Implement traffic shaping by user type. Task: (a) Regular users (x-client: browser) → full speed, no limits. (b) Batch jobs (x-client: batch-job) → 10 req/s + 100ms delay. (c) Write EnvoyFilter matching on header value. (d) Test with both headers. (e) Explain: this is traffic SHAPING — different classes get different limits, like express lanes vs regular lanes.
Show Answer
Answer

EnvoyFilter with header match: x-client: batch-job → rate limit 10 req/s + delay. Without matching header → pass through at full speed. Priority lanes for real users, throttled lanes for batch jobs.

Explanation

Traffic shaping = different limits per traffic class. Match on headers to classify requests at the proxy level.

Q5
Explain the global rate limiting architecture. Task: Draw the flow: Envoy → gRPC → Rate Limit Service → Redis (INCR + TTL). If count > limit → 429 + Retry-After. If count ≤ limit → 200, forwarded to Django. Explain: Redis is the shared counter, gRPC adds per-request latency (~1-5ms). The rate limit service is NOT built into Istio — it's a separate deployment.
Show Answer
Answer

Envoy → gRPC check(IP, path) → Rate Limit Service → Redis INCR key → if > limit → 429 with Retry-After. Redis key TTL = rate limit window. External deployment required.

Explanation

Global RL = Redis requirement. The rate limit service is separate from Istio. gRPC check adds latency per request.

Q6
Compare token bucket vs leaky bucket. Task: Token bucket (Envoy): tokens refill at fixed rate, burst allowed until empty, then 429. Burst-friendly — good for web traffic. Leaky bucket: requests queue at constant rate, excess overflows. Smooth output, no bursts. Envoy uses token bucket with maxTokens (burst) and tokensPerFill (rate).
Show Answer
Answer

Token bucket = burst allowed (maxTokens=20, tokensPerFill=10, fillInterval=1s). Leaky bucket = constant rate, no bursts. Envoy uses token bucket.

Explanation

Token bucket is burst-friendly (web spikes). Leaky bucket smooths (consistent-rate processing). Know which Envoy uses.

Q7
Shape traffic: batch jobs get throttled while users get full speed. Task: Write EnvoyFilter that matches header x-client: batch-job → applies 10 req/s + 100ms delay. Regular users (no header or x-client: browser) pass at full speed. Explain: this protects user-facing Django from being overwhelmed by batch processing.
Show Answer
Answer

EnvoyFilter: match header → apply rate limit + delay. Unmatched → full speed. Header-based traffic classification at proxy level.

Explanation

Protect user traffic from batch jobs by applying different rate limits based on request headers.

Q8
Understand EnvoyFilter CRD. Task: Explain key fields: workloadSelector (which pods), configPatches (Envoy config changes), applyTo (HTTP_FILTER, NETWORK_FILTER, LISTENER, CLUSTER, ROUTE). EnvoyFilter directly patches raw Envoy config — most powerful and potentially dangerous CRD. Use for: rate limiting, Lua filters, header manipulation, WASM plugins.
Show Answer
Answer

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3, kind: EnvoyFilter. Directly modifies Envoy proxy configuration. Most powerful Istio CRD.

Explanation

EnvoyFilter = raw Envoy config patching. For local rate limiting, custom filters, WASM. Be careful — incorrect patches break proxies.

Q9
Pod 2 hits rate limit (429), Pods 1 and 3 are idle. Task: (a) Pod 2 at limit → 429 for Pod 2 only. (b) Pods 1 and 3 serve normally (independent buckets). (c) Total capacity = 3 × limit, but distribution isn't guaranteed. (d) This is local RL's tradeoff: no shared state (no Redis dependency) but uneven distribution possible. Global RL solves uneven distribution but requires Redis.
Show Answer
Answer

Local RL: each pod has independent bucket. One pod at limit doesn't affect others. Total = pods × limit, distribution not guaranteed.

Explanation

Local = independent (no SPOF, uneven distribution). Global = shared counter (accurate, requires Redis). Trade-off.

Q10
Comprehensive rate limiting drill. Task: (a) Apply local RL (100 req/s per pod) to jobpost-api via EnvoyFilter. (b) Test: 150 req → ~100 succeed, ~50 get 429. (c) Verify Kiali/Prometheus shows 429 responses. (d) Add traffic shaping: batch jobs → 10 req/s + 100ms delay. (e) Test with x-client: batch-job → 10 succeed then 429. (f) Remove RL configs. Write all YAML and verify commands.
Show Answer
Answer

Apply EnvoyFilter → test 429 threshold → verify in Prometheus (istio_requests_total{response_code=\"429\"}) → add shaping → test → cleanup.

Explanation

Complete rate limiting workflow: apply, test threshold, observe metrics, shape traffic, cleanup.

Span Istio across multiple Kubernetes clusters, add legacy VMs to the mesh, and explore the new ambient mesh — sidecar-free Istio with 6× less memory overhead.

🎯 What You'll Learn

  • ✅ Understand multi-cluster deployment models: Primary-Remote vs Multi-Primary vs External CP
  • ✅ Enable cross-cluster mTLS via shared root CA and east-west gateways
  • ✅ Add legacy VMs/bare-metal servers to the mesh using WorkloadEntry + WorkloadGroup
  • ✅ Explore ambient mesh: sidecar-free Istio with ztunnel (L4) + waypoint proxy (L7)

💡 ICA Exam Tips for Chapter 16
  • "Multi-cluster production" = Multi-Primary (each cluster has own istiod, no SPOF)
  • "Cross-cluster traffic" = East-west gateway (NOT the same as ingress gateway)
  • "Add a VM to mesh" = WorkloadEntry (IP + labels + serviceAccount) + WorkloadGroup
  • "Reduce resource usage" = Ambient mesh (ztunnel per-node, ~50Mi shared vs ~128Mi per pod)
  • "Enable ambient" = Label namespace istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient (NOT istio-injection)
  • Ambient L4 = always on (ztunnel), L7 = optional (waypoint per namespace)

16.1 Multi-Cluster Istio — Spanning Kubernetes Clusters

Single mesh across EU + US clusters with locality-based routing — EU users go to EU cluster, auto-failover to US if EU is down. mTLS works seamlessly across clusters.

🌍 MULTI-CLUSTER — anihpj EU + US
🌍 EU Users                                    🌎 US Users
     │                                               │
[EU LoadBalancer]                            [US LoadBalancer]
     │                                               │
┌────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────┐
│                        SINGLE ISTIO MESH                              │
│  CLUSTER 1 (EU — Frankfurt)    │    CLUSTER 2 (US — Virginia)         │
│  istiod (EU primary)           │    istiod (US replica)               │
│  jobpost-api:v1 · user-service │    jobpost-api:v1 · user-service     │
│       │    mTLS cross-cluster ─┼─────────┘                            │
│                                                                       │
│  VirtualService: locality-based failover                              │
│  • EU users → EU cluster (low latency)                               │
│  • EU cluster down → auto failover to US cluster                     │
Primary-Remote

One istiod manages both clusters. Simpler but single point of failure.

Multi-Primary

Each cluster has own istiod. Recommended for production.

External CP

istiod outside any cluster. Advanced setup for managed services.

16.2 VM Workloads in the Mesh

Add legacy VMs (databases, monoliths) to the Istio mesh. The VM gets a SPIFFE certificate and is treated like a Pod — full mTLS, metrics, and authorization policies.

yaml — WorkloadEntry: Register a VM 

# Register legacy PostgreSQL VM in the mesh
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: WorkloadEntry
metadata:
  name: postgres-vm
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  address: 10.0.5.20           # VM IP address
  labels:
    app: postgres              # Labels for policy matching
  serviceAccount: postgres-sa  # For SPIFFE identity

# Result: skills-service → PostgreSQL VM over mTLS!
# VM gets cert from istiod, metrics in Grafana,
# AuthorizationPolicy controls who can query it.

16.3 Istio Ambient Mesh — Sidecar-Free Mode

New architecture: no sidecar injection required! ztunnel (per-node) handles L4 mTLS, waypoint proxy handles L7 features per namespace. 6× less memory overhead.

🏗️ SIDECAR vs AMBIENT

Sidecar ModeAmbient Mode
ArchitectureEnvoy proxy per podztunnel per NODE (shared)
Memory per pod~128Mi~0Mi (shared)
7 anihpj services7 × 128Mi = ~900Mi1 ztunnel = ~50Mi
L7 featuresBuilt-in per sidecarOptional waypoint proxy
Pod startup+50ms (sidecar)No overhead
Pod READY2/2 (app + sidecar)1/1 (app only!)
bash — Enable ambient mode for anihpj 

# Install Istio with ambient profile
istioctl install --set profile=ambient -y

# Enable ambient for namespace (no istio-injection label!)
kubectl label namespace anihpj istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient

# Result: pods in anihpj get L4 mTLS via ztunnel automatically
# No 2/2 — pods stay at 1/1!

16.4 Ambient Mesh Architecture — How ztunnel and Waypoint Work Together

From the official docs: Ambient mesh splits Istio's functionality into two layers — a zero-trust secure overlay (ztunnel for L4) and an optional L7 processing layer (waypoint proxy). This layered approach is what gives ambient its 6× memory savings.

🏗️ AMBIENT MESH ARCHITECTURE — Two-Layer Design
🔒
LAYER 1: ztunnel (L4 — Always On)

One ztunnel pod per Kubernetes Node. Handles: mTLS encryption, simple L4 authorization, TCP metrics, and traffic routing at TCP level. Written in Rust for performance. No per-pod overhead. Every pod on the node shares one ztunnel.

🧠
LAYER 2: Waypoint Proxy (L7 — Optional)

One Envoy-based waypoint deployment per namespace (or per service account). Handles: VirtualService routing, retries, timeouts, circuit breaking, L7 AuthorizationPolicy, telemetry. Only deploy if you need L7 features.

🔄 AMBIENT TRAFFIC FLOW — How a Request Travels
  L4 ONLY (no waypoint):                     L7 (with waypoint):
                                        
  Pod A ──▶ ztunnel(Node1) ──▶ Pod B        Pod A ──▶ ztunnel ──▶ waypoint ──▶ ztunnel ──▶ Pod B
  (app)    (mTLS, L4 authz)  (app)          (app)    (mTLS)    (VS routing,  (mTLS)    (app)
                                                    │          retries, CB)           │
                                                    │                                  │
  ✅ mTLS encryption                          ✅ mTLS + L4 authz                      │
  ✅ L4 authz (basic allow/deny)             ✅ VS weight-based routing               │
  ✅ TCP metrics                             ✅ Retries, timeouts, CB                 │
  ❌ HTTP routing (URI/headers)              ✅ L7 AuthorizationPolicy                │
  ❌ Retries, timeouts, circuit breaker      ✅ Full telemetry (RED metrics)          │

🚀 AMBIENT MIGRATION — Sidecar → Ambient Coexistence

StepActionResult
1Install Istio with ambient profileztunnel DaemonSet runs on all nodes
2Label test namespace: istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambientPods get L4 mTLS via ztunnel, no sidecars
3Verify: kubectl get pods shows 1/1No istio-proxy container needed!
4Deploy waypoint if L7 needed: istioctl waypoint apply -n anihpjPer-namespace Envoy for L7 features
5Gradually migrate namespaces from sidecar to ambientBoth modes coexist seamlessly
6Remove istio-injection=enabled from migrated namespacesClean cutover from sidecar to ambient

16.X Deep Dive — Sidecar vs Ambient: Decision Guide

⚖️ WHEN TO CHOOSE WHICH MODE
SIDECAR: When you need
  • ALL L7 features: VS routing, retries, CB, fault injection
  • Per-pod metrics granularity
  • Custom Envoy filters (Lua, WASM)
  • Standard production workloads (~128Mi/pod)
AMBIENT: When you need
  • Resource efficiency (~50Mi/node vs ~128Mi/pod)
  • Simpler ops: no sidecar injection management
  • L4 mTLS + basic authz sufficient
  • Fast pod startup (no init container wait)
  • Gradual migration: coexist with sidecar mode

16.Y Deep Dive — HBONE: HTTP-Based Overlay Network Encapsulation

From the official Istio ambient mesh architecture docs: HBONE (HTTP-Based Overlay Network Encapsulation) is the secure tunneling protocol that replaces iptables-based traffic interception in ambient mode. It's how ztunnel transparently encrypts and routes traffic without sidecars.

🔗 HBONE TUNNEL — How Traffic Flows Through Ambient Mesh
  SIDECAR MODE (iptables):
  App:3000 → iptables REDIRECT → localhost:15001 → Envoy (mTLS) → network
  
  AMBIENT MODE (HBONE):
  App:3000 → Node network → ztunnel:15008 (HBONE) → remote ztunnel → App:3000
  
  HBONE PROTOCOL STACK:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Application Data (HTTP/gRPC/TCP)│  ← Your app's payload
  ├──────────────────────────────────┤
  │  HTTP/2 CONNECT tunnel (HBONE)   │  ← Encapsulation layer
  ├──────────────────────────────────┤
  │  mTLS (SPIFFE certs)             │  ← Identity & encryption
  ├──────────────────────────────────┤
  │  TCP/IP                           │  ← Network transport
  └──────────────────────────────────┘
  
  KEY PROPERTIES:
  • Uses HTTP/2 CONNECT method to create tunnel (like WebSocket-over-HTTP/2)
  • Encrypts via mTLS using SPIFFE identities (same as sidecar mode)
  • ztunnel terminates HBONE on both ends (source ztunnel → dest ztunnel)
  • No iptables needed — ztunnel captures via eBPF or policy routing
  • Transparent to applications — no code changes, no sidecars
💡 Why HBONE Instead of iptables?

iptables requires per-pod rules, root privileges (NET_ADMIN), and init containers — the sidecar model. HBONE uses standard HTTP/2 tunneling between ztunnels on each node — no per-pod rules, no init containers, no root access to pod network namespace. This is what makes ambient mesh 6× lighter: one ztunnel per node handles all pods on that node via HBONE tunnels.

Q1
Register a legacy PostgreSQL VM (10.0.5.20:5432) in the mesh. Task: (a) Write a WorkloadEntry with IP, labels (app: postgres), and serviceAccount. (b) Write a ServiceEntry for postgres.internal.example.com with MESH_INTERNAL location. (c) Write a DestinationRule with ISTIO_MUTUAL TLS mode. (d) Verify: VM gets SPIFFE cert from istiod, appears in Kiali. Full mesh policies (mTLS, Authz, metrics) apply.
Show Answer
Answer

WorkloadEntry (IP + labels + SA) + ServiceEntry (MESH_INTERNAL + STATIC) = VM in mesh. Gets SPIFFE identity, participates in mTLS.

Explanation

WorkloadEntry bridges non-K8s workloads into the mesh. VM needs istio-proxy + network access to istiod:15012.

Q2
Compare sidecar vs ambient mesh. Task: (a) Calculate overhead: sidecar = 7 × 128Mi = ~900Mi for anihpj. Ambient = 1 ztunnel per node = ~50Mi shared. (b) Enable ambient: kubectl label ns anihpj istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient (NOT istio-injection). (c) Verify: pods show 1/1, no istio-proxy container. (d) L7 features require per-namespace waypoint proxy. (e) Sidecar+ambient coexist — migrate namespace by namespace.
Show Answer
Answer

Ambient = 6× less memory. ztunnel (per-node, L4) + optional waypoint (per-ns, L7). No sidecar injection. Pods stay 1/1. Coexistence with sidecar mode.

Explanation

Ambient is Istio's newer lighter architecture. ztunnel = Rust-based per-node proxy. Waypoint = optional per-namespace Envoy for L7.

Q3
Design multi-cluster Istio. Task: (a) Compare: Primary-Remote (one istiod, simpler, SPOF) vs Multi-Primary (each cluster has istiod, recommended for production). (b) Explain cross-cluster mTLS: shared root CA, SPIFFE identities globally unique, east-west gateway for traffic. (c) Locality-based routing: EU users → EU cluster, auto-failover to US. Configured in DestinationRule.
Show Answer
Answer

Production: Multi-Primary (no SPOF). Cross-cluster mTLS via shared root CA. East-west gateway for cross-cluster traffic. Locality routing via DestinationRule.

Explanation

Multi-cluster: Multi-Primary for production. East-west gateway ≠ ingress gateway. mTLS works seamlessly across clusters.

Q4
Verify cross-cluster mTLS. Task: (a) All clusters share root CA (auto-created). (b) SPIFFE identities include cluster info — globally unique. (c) East-west gateway handles cross-cluster routing. (d) mTLS handshake between services in different clusters — transparent to applications. (e) No additional config needed beyond multi-cluster setup.
Show Answer
Answer

Shared root CA = cross-cluster mTLS works automatically. SPIFFE IDs are globally unique. East-west gateway routes cross-cluster traffic.

Explanation

Cross-cluster mTLS is transparent — same root CA, different clusters, seamless encryption.

Q5
Enable ambient mesh for anihpj. Task: (a) Install Istio: istioctl install --set profile=ambient -y. (b) Label namespace: kubectl label ns anihpj istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient. (c) Verify: ztunnel DaemonSet running, pods show 1/1, mTLS working (Kiali locks). (d) Different from sidecar: different label, different profile, no istio-init, no iptables. (e) Add waypoint for L7: istioctl waypoint apply -n anihpj.
Show Answer
Answer

Ambient: profile=ambient, label=istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient, pods stay 1/1. Optional waypoint for L7 features. Coexists with sidecar mode.

Explanation

Key differences: label key, install profile, pod count (1/1 vs 2/2), no iptables, ztunnel per-node.

Q6
Explain cross-cluster service discovery. Task: Each istiod discovers local services via K8s API. Clusters exchange endpoints via east-west gateway. DNS resolves cross-cluster services to gateway IP. Envoy routes through gateway with mTLS. Locality-based routing: prefer local cluster, failover to remote.
Show Answer
Answer

Local discovery via K8s API → endpoint exchange via east-west gateway → DNS resolution → mTLS routing. Locality LB for geo-routing.

Explanation

East-west gateway = cross-cluster traffic. Separate from north-south (ingress) gateway.

Q7
Configure locality-based routing. Task: Route EU users to EU cluster, US users to US cluster. DestinationRule: trafficPolicy.loadBalancer.localityLbSetting.enabled: true. Uses node labels topology.istio.io/subzone. Auto-failover: if EU cluster down → traffic routes to US. Goal: minimize latency by keeping traffic in-region.
Show Answer
Answer

DestinationRule → localityLbSetting.enabled=true. EU users → EU cluster. US users → US cluster. Auto-failover on zone failure.

Explanation

Locality-based routing = keep traffic close to users. DestinationRule feature. Uses node topology labels.

Q8
VM gets SPIFFE cert from istiod. Task: Register via WorkloadEntry + WorkloadGroup. Install istio-proxy on VM. VM's Envoy → CSR to istiod:15012 → istiod validates WorkloadEntry → signs SVID cert. VM now has SPIFFE identity, participates in mTLS, appears in Kiali, subject to AuthorizationPolicy.
Show Answer
Answer

WorkloadEntry → WorkloadGroup → install proxy → CSR → istiod validation → SVID issued. Full mesh participation for VMs.

Explanation

Bridge legacy infrastructure into mesh. VM needs: proxy installed, network to istiod:15012, WorkloadEntry registration.

Q9
Ambient mesh L4 vs L7. Task: ztunnel (L4, always on): mTLS, L4 authz, TCP metrics. Waypoint (L7, optional per-namespace): VirtualService routing, retries, timeouts, circuit breaking, L7 AuthorizationPolicy, full telemetry. Without waypoint = L4 only. With waypoint = L4 + L7. Deploy waypoint only for namespaces that need L7 features.
Show Answer
Answer

ztunnel = L4 (mTLS + basic authz + TCP metrics), always on. Waypoint = L7 (VS routing + retries + CB + L7 authz), optional per-ns.

Explanation

Ambient layers: ztunnel (free, always on) + waypoint (opt-in, per-namespace). Add L7 only where needed.

Q10
Sidecar + ambient coexistence. Task: (a) Some namespaces use sidecar (istio-injection=enabled). (b) Some use ambient (istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient). (c) Traffic between them: mTLS works seamlessly via shared root CA. (d) Kiali shows both types — nodes with sidecars and nodes without. (e) Migrate gradually: label one namespace ambient, verify, move to next. No big-bang needed.
Show Answer
Answer

Sidecar + ambient coexist in same cluster. mTLS between them works. Migrate ns by ns. No big-bang required.

Explanation

Coexistence is an ambient design feature. Gradual migration: label ns ambient → verify → next ns. Both modes work together.

Troubleshooting 15% Operations ALL DOMAINS

17.1 Upgrading Istio — Safely in Production

Istio releases every ~3 months. NEVER use istioctl upgrade (in-place) in production. Use canary upgrade — run old and new istiod simultaneously.

🔄 CANARY ISTIO UPGRADE — Old + New istiod in Parallel
1
Install New istiod

istioctl install --set revision=1-22
Both old + new run side-by-side

2
Label Test NS

kubectl label ns anihpj-test istio.io/rev=1-22
Test namespace uses new istiod

3
Validate

Check Kiali, Grafana, proxy-status
All SYNCED with new istiod? ✅

4
Migrate Prod NS

Label anihpj → istio.io/rev=1-22
Rolling restart pods → new sidecars

5
Remove Old

All namespaces migrated → delete old istiod
✅ Upgrade complete, zero downtime!

17.3 High Availability for istiod

Run 3 istiod replicas across availability zones with PodDisruptionBudget. If istiod goes down: existing proxies KEEP working with cached config.

🏗️ istiod HA — 3 Replicas Across Zones
Zone A

istiod replica 1
Node 1 → sidecars

Zone B

istiod replica 2
Node 2 → sidecars

Zone C

istiod replica 3
Node 3 → sidecars

bash — Scale istiod for HA 

# Scale istiod to 3 replicas
kubectl patch deployment istiod -n istio-system \
  -p '{"spec":{"replicas":3}}'

# Apply PodDisruptionBudget (min 2 available)
kubectl create pdb istiod-pdb -n istio-system \
  --selector=app=istiod --min-available=2

# If Zone A fails: replicas 2+3 take over
# Existing proxies: KEEP WORKING with cached config ✅

17.X Deep Dive — Production Operational Patterns: Day-2 Operations

Beyond installation, production Istio requires Day-2 operational discipline. Here are the patterns that keep your mesh healthy:

🔄 1. Canary Istio Upgrade — The Only Safe Way
ISTIO UPGRADE — Canary Pattern Step-by-Step
  1. istioctl install --set revision=1-23 -y       ← NEW istiod alongside old
  2. kubectl get pods -n istio-system              ← 2 istiods: istiod AND istiod-1-23
  3. kubectl label ns test istio.io/rev=1-23       ← Test namespace first
  4. kubectl rollout restart deploy -n test         ← Recreate pods → get new sidecar
  5. istioctl proxy-status | grep test              ← Verify ALL SYNCED on 1-23
  6. RUN TESTS → VALIDATE → APPROVE
  7. For each prod ns: label & restart (one by one)
  8. istioctl uninstall --revision=OLD             ← Remove old istiod
  ⚡ ROLLBACK: kubectl label ns prod istio.io/rev-  ← Remove label → instant rollback
📊 2. Resource Monitoring — What to Watch
Sidecar Memory

Soft limit: 128Mi. Alert at 200Mi. Proxy wasm filters add ~10-30Mi each. Restart if leak suspected.

istiod CPU

1vCPU per 500 sidecars. Scale horizontally (3 replicas for HA). Watch xDS push latency.

Config Volume

>1000 VS/DR = consider Sidecar resource to limit config push. Each service ~5KB config per proxy.

🔧 3. Emergency Diagnostic Checklist
  1. istioctl analyze -A                    ← 80% of issues found here (YAML validation)
  2. istioctl proxy-status                  ← ALL proxies synced? STALE = config push failure
  3. kubectl logs -l app=istiod -n istio-system --tail=100 | grep -i error
  4. istioctl proxy-config cluster deploy/X | grep   ← Endpoint discovery?
  5. istioctl proxy-config route deploy/X                     ← Are routes correct?
  6. istioctl proxy-config listener deploy/X                  ← Ports open?
  7. kubectl get peerauthentication,authorizationpolicy -A    ← Policy conflicts?
  8. istioctl authn tls-check deploy/X -n Y                   ← mTLS working?
⚠️ ICA: High-Availability Architecture

Production istiod: 3 replicas with PodDisruptionBudget(minAvailable=2) spread across nodes (topologySpreadConstraints). Set resource limits: 2Gi RAM, 2 CPU. Configure HPA: min 3, max 5, CPU 80%. Ingress gateway: 2+ replicas with external LoadBalancer.

17.X Common Problems & Best Practices — ICA Troubleshooting Reference

From the official Istio operations guide, here is a structured reference for the most common problems you'll encounter on the ICA exam and in production:

✅ Production Best Practices (from official docs)
Deployment
  • Use revisioned control planes for upgrades
  • 3 istiod replicas + PDB(minAvailable=2)
  • Set resource limits: 2Gi RAM, 2 CPU per istiod
  • Never use istioctl upgrade in production
  • Enable meshConfig.defaultConfig.holdApplicationUntilProxyStarts
Traffic
  • Always add retries to VirtualServices
  • Set timeouts shorter than application timeouts
  • Use CircuitBreakers for every upstream
  • Prefer header-based routing over weight for canary
  • Validate with istioctl analyze before apply
Security
  • STRICT mTLS for all production namespaces
  • AuthorizationPolicy: default DENY, then ALLOW
  • Rotate root cert before expiry (365d default)
  • Use separate namespaces for different trust domains
  • Sign Istio images for supply chain security

📝 Chapter 17 — ICA Practice Questions (Hands-On Lab Scenarios)

Q1
Your VirtualService isn't routing. Task: Run istioctl analyze -n anihpj FIRST — catches 80% of errors. Check: (a) DR subsets match pod labels? (b) Port names start with http/grpc/tcp/tls? (c) VS hosts match Gateway hosts? (d) istioctl proxy-status — all SYNCED? (e) istioctl proxy-config route deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj — VS rules in Envoy? Fix the most common cause: DR subset labels don't match pod labels.
Show Answer
Answer
istioctl analyze -n anihpj  # ALWAYS FIRST
istioctl proxy-status       # Check sync
istioctl proxy-config route deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj  # Actual Envoy routes
kubectl get pods -n anihpj --show-labels  # Check subset labels

Top 3 causes: DR subset labels mismatch, port names missing protocol prefix, VS host mismatch.

Explanation

istioctl analyze is ALWAYS the first troubleshooting step on the ICA exam. Catches ~80% of errors before deep debugging.

Q2
Debug mTLS issues — services getting 503. Task: (a) istioctl authn tls-check deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj — shows cert, trust chain, mTLS per-port. (b) Check PeerAuthentication mode (STRICT?). (c) Check DestinationRule TLS mode (ISTIO_MUTUAL?). (d) istioctl proxy-config secret deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj — verify cert exists. (e) Align DR/PA: both sides must agree on TLS.
Show Answer
Answer

DR = client side (what outbound Envoy sends). PA = server side (what inbound Envoy requires). ISTIO_MUTUAL + STRICT = working mTLS. Mismatch = 503.

Explanation

TLS contract: DR decides what to send, PA decides what to accept. Both must be compatible. Check both with istioctl authn tls-check.

Q3
Safely upgrade Istio in production. Task: (a) NEVER use istioctl upgrade (in-place, no rollback). (b) Canary upgrade: istioctl install --set revision=1-22 — old+new istiod parallel. (c) Label test ns: kubectl label ns test istio.io/rev=1-22. (d) Verify proxy-status all SYNCED. (e) Migrate prod ns one by one. (f) Remove old istiod only after all migrated. (g) Rollback: remove revision label — instant.
Show Answer
Answer

Canary upgrade: install new revision parallel → label test ns → validate → migrate prod ns one by one → remove old istiod. Rollback: unlabel ns.

Explanation

Canary upgrade = production standard. Old+new istiod coexist. Rollback = remove revision label. Never use istioctl upgrade in prod.

Q4
istiod goes down — what happens? Task: (a) Existing proxies KEEP WORKING with cached config. (b) Traffic continues flowing. (c) Only NEW pods (new sidecars) and config CHANGES fail. (d) Run 3 istiod replicas + PDB(minAvailable=2) for HA. (e) Explain: control/data plane separation = control plane failure does NOT cause data plane outage.
Show Answer
Answer

Control plane down = existing data plane keeps working. Only new pods and config changes affected. 3 replicas + PDB for HA.

Explanation

Architectural resilience: Envoy caches last-known-good config. istiod failure ≠ traffic outage. This is a key ICA concept.

Q5
Calculate resource requirements. Task: Each sidecar = ~128Mi RAM + ~100m CPU. anihpj (7 services): ~900Mi + ~700m CPU. Dev (10 pods): ~2Gi. Small Prod (50): ~8Gi. Medium Prod (100): ~15Gi. Large Prod (500): ~67Gi. istiod: 1-3 replicas, 500m-3c CPU, 2-12Gi RAM. Ambient alternative: ~50Mi per node (6× less).
Show Answer
Answer

Sidecar = 128Mi/pod rule of thumb. Plan cluster capacity: dev ~2Gi, small prod ~8Gi, medium ~15Gi, large ~67Gi. Ambient = 6× less memory.

Explanation

Resource planning is critical for production. Know the 128Mi per sidecar rule. Ambient mesh dramatically reduces overhead.

Q6
Top 3 VirtualService routing failures. Task: (1) DR subsets don't match pod labels → check kubectl get pods --show-labels. (2) Port names missing protocol prefix → check Service port names start with http/grpc/tcp/tls. (3) VS hosts don't match Service/Gateway → align hosts across all resources. All caught by istioctl analyze. Fix in this order.
Show Answer
Answer

#1: subset labels mismatch. #2: port name without protocol prefix. #3: host mismatch. All caught by istioctl analyze.

Explanation

These 3 cover ~80% of routing failures. Always check in this order. istioctl analyze catches all three.

Q7
Integrate Istio validation into CI/CD. Task: (a) Store Istio CRDs alongside app manifests in Git. (b) Run istioctl analyze -f istio/ --failure-threshold WARNING in CI. (c) Block PR if analysis fails. (d) Use ArgoCD/Flux for GitOps — sync Gateway, VS, DR, PA, Authz with deployments. (e) Catch config errors BEFORE production. Shift-left Istio validation.
Show Answer
Answer

CI: istioctl analyze -f istio/ → block PR on failure. GitOps: Istio CRDs version-controlled alongside app manifests. Shift-left validation.

Explanation

Catch Istio config errors before they hit production. GitOps + istioctl analyze in CI = production best practice.

Q8
Production go-live checklist. Task: Verify ALL 9 items: (1) Pods 2/2, (2) proxy-status all SYNCED, (3) istioctl analyze 0 errors, (4) STRICT mTLS, (5) Authz policies tested, (6) All VS routes working, (7) istiod HA (3 replicas + PDB), (8) Tracing sampling 1%, (9) Alerts set (err>1%, p99>500ms). Write the verification command for each.
Show Answer
Answer

9-item checklist: pods 2/2, proxy SYNCED, analyze 0 errors, STRICT mTLS, Authz tested, routes working, istiod HA, sampling 1%, alerts set.

Explanation

Complete go-live checklist. Run all 9 before declaring production-ready. Each item has a specific verification command.

Q9
Essential troubleshooting commands. Task: Memorize these 7 commands: (1) istioctl analyze -n anihpj — config errors. (2) istioctl proxy-status — sync state. (3) istioctl authn tls-check deploy/X -n Y — mTLS. (4) kubectl get ns --show-labels — injection label. (5) istioctl pc route deploy/X -n Y — Envoy routes. (6) istioctl pc endpoint deploy/X -n Y — endpoints. (7) istioctl dashboard kiali — topology.
Show Answer
Answer

7 essential commands: analyze → proxy-status → authn tls-check → ns labels → pc route → pc endpoint → dashboard kiali. In that order.

Explanation

ICA exam troubleshooting toolkit. Always start with analyze. These 7 commands cover 95% of Istio debugging scenarios.

Q10
Comprehensive production ops drill. Task: (a) Run the 9-item go-live checklist. (b) Simulate a VirtualService routing failure — debug with analyze + pc route. (c) Simulate mTLS failure — debug with authn tls-check. (d) Perform canary upgrade of istiod (old+new parallel). (e) Verify HA: kill one istiod pod, confirm traffic continues. (f) Rollback upgrade by removing revision label. Write all commands.
Show Answer
Answer

Checklist → break VS → debug with analyze → fix → break mTLS → debug with tls-check → fix → canary upgrade → HA test → rollback.

Complete production operations workflow. Know everything: upgrade, debug, HA, rollback, checklist. This is the ICA exam capstone.

📋 ICA Exam Format

Duration: 2 hours | Format: Hands-on CLI tasks in a live Istio + Kubernetes environment | Open Book: Yes — you can access istio.io/docs during the exam | Passing Score: ~75%

🔑 TOP 20 MUST-KNOW COMMANDS & FACTS FOR ICA
1. Install Istio

istioctl install --set profile=demo -y

2. Enable Injection

kubectl label ns X istio-injection=enabled

3. Check Injection

kubectl get pods → MUST show 2/2

4. Validate Config

istioctl analyze -n <ns> — catches 80% of errors!

5. Check Sync

istioctl proxy-status → all SYNCED

6. Gateway + VS Rule

Gateway WITHOUT VirtualService = traffic DROPPED

7. Port Names

MUST be "http"/"grpc"/"tcp"/"tls" — Istio uses port NAME not number

8. Canary Pattern

VS: weight v1=90, v2=10 + DR: subsets v1/v2

9. mTLS STRICT

PeerAuthentication: spec.mtls.mode: STRICT

10. Deny All

AuthorizationPolicy: spec: {} = deny everything

11. Circuit Breaker

DR outlierDetection.consecutiveGatewayErrors: 5

12. Retries

VS retries: {attempts: 3, perTryTimeout: 2s} — idempotent only!

13. External APIs

ServiceEntry: location: MESH_EXTERNAL, resolution: DNS

14. Mirror Traffic

VS mirror: {host: X, subset: v2} — v2 gets silent copy

15. Pod Labels

app: X AND version: v1 — REQUIRED for subsets!

16. Debug mTLS

istioctl authn tls-check <pod> -n <ns>

17. Inspect Envoy

istioctl proxy-config cluster <pod> -n <ns>

18. Open Dashboards

istioctl dashboard kiali / grafana / jaeger

19. Sidecar NOT injected?

Namespace label missing OR pod existed before labeling

20. VS not routing?

DR subsets don't match pod labels → 503 errors

⚠️ TOP 10 ICA EXAM MISTAKES — Avoid These!
#MistakeWhy It Costs PointsCorrect Approach
1Forgetting port name prefixIstio treats as TCP, all L7 features disabledAlways use "http"/"grpc"/"tcp"/"tls"
2Gateway without VirtualServiceTraffic accepted but DROPPED — 404Always pair GW with VS via gateways field
3Missing version label on podsDR subsets resolve to ZERO endpoints → 503Add labels: {app: X, version: v1}
4Not running istioctl analyzeConfig errors go undetectedALWAYS run analyze before considering done
5Using istioctl upgrade in prodIn-place upgrade risks downtimeAlways canary upgrade: old+new istiod
6Not forwarding tracing headersBroken traces — isolated spans onlyPropagate x-b3-* headers in all HTTP calls
7mTLS without AuthzPolicyAny service can call any servicemTLS = identity, AuthzPolicy = permissions
8Retries on non-idempotent requestsDouble-charge payments, duplicate recordsOnly retry GET; use retryOn: 5xx only
9retries × perTryTimeout > timeoutTimeout fires before retries completeAlways: retries × perTryTimeout < timeout
10REGISTRY_ONLY without ServiceEntriesAll external APIs blocked with 502Create ServiceEntry BEFORE switching mode

📎 Appendix B: Complete anihpj Istio YAML Manifests

B.1 Namespace Setup

yaml — Namespace with Istio injection enabled 

apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: anihpj
  labels:
    istio-injection: enabled    # ← KEY: enables auto sidecar injection
    environment: production
---
# Verify:
# kubectl get namespace anihpj --show-labels
# NAME      STATUS   LABELS
# anihpj    Active   istio-injection=enabled,environment=prod

B.2 Dockerfile for anihpj/jobpost-api

dockerfile — anihpj/jobpost/Dockerfile 

FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies (Docker layer cache optimization)
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy application code
COPY . .
RUN python manage.py collectstatic --noinput

# Health check (required for K8s liveness probe)
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/health/ || exit 1

EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["gunicorn", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000",
     "--workers", "4", "--timeout", "120",
     "anihpj.wsgi:application"]

# Build: docker build -t anihpj/jobpost-api:v1 .
# Push:  docker push anihpj/jobpost-api:v1

B.3 Complete Deployment + Service

yaml — Deployment + Service for jobpost-api 

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: jobpost-api
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: jobpost-api
      version: v1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: jobpost-api      # ← REQUIRED for Istio/Kiali
        version: v1           # ← REQUIRED for canary subsets
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: jobpost
        image: anihpj/jobpost-api:v1
        ports:
        - name: http          # ← REQUIRED: Istio uses port name
          containerPort: 8000
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health/
            port: 8000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: jobpost-api           # ← VirtualService references this
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:
    app: jobpost-api          # ← matches Deployment label
  ports:
  - name: http                # ← MUST be "http"
    port: 80
    targetPort: 8000

B.4-B.13 — Gateway, VirtualService, DestinationRule, PeerAuthentication, AuthorizationPolicy, ServiceEntry, RequestAuthentication, and Telemetry are covered in detail within their respective chapters.

B.4 Istio Gateway for anihpj.example.com

yaml — anihpj-gateway.yaml 

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: anihpj-gateway
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:
    istio: ingressgateway
  servers:
  - port:
      number: 80
      name: http
      protocol: HTTP
    hosts:
    - "anihpj.example.com"
  - port:
      number: 443
      name: https
      protocol: HTTPS
    tls:
      mode: SIMPLE
      credentialName: anihpj-tls-cert
    hosts:
    - "anihpj.example.com"

B.5 VirtualService — Path-Based Routing

yaml — path-based routing for all services 

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: anihpj-routes
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  gateways:
  - anihpj-gateway
  hosts:
  - "anihpj.example.com"
  http:
  - match:
    - uri:
        prefix: /jobs/
    route:
    - destination:
        host: jobpost-api
  - match:
    - uri:
        prefix: /users/
    route:
    - destination:
        host: user-service
  - match:
    - uri:
        prefix: /skills/
    route:
    - destination:
        host: skills-service
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: jobpost-api

B.6 VirtualService — Canary (90/10 Split)

yaml — canary deployment for jobpost-api 

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: jobpost-api-vs
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  hosts:
  - jobpost-api
  http:
  - route:
    - destination:
        host: jobpost-api
        subset: v1
      weight: 90
    - destination:
        host: jobpost-api
        subset: v2
      weight: 10

B.7 DestinationRule — Subsets, LEAST_CONN, Circuit Breaker

yaml — DestinationRule for jobpost-api 

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: jobpost-api-dr
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  host: jobpost-api
  trafficPolicy:
    loadBalancer:
      simple: LEAST_CONN
    connectionPool:
      tcp:
        maxConnections: 100
      http:
        http1MaxPendingRequests: 50
    outlierDetection:
      consecutiveGatewayErrors: 5
      interval: 30s
      baseEjectionTime: 30s
      maxEjectionPercent: 50
    tls:
      mode: ISTIO_MUTUAL
  subsets:
  - name: v1
    labels:
      version: v1
  - name: v2
    labels:
      version: v2

B.8 PeerAuthentication — STRICT mTLS

yaml — PeerAuthentication for anihpj 

apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT

B.9 AuthorizationPolicy — Deny-All Baseline

yaml — deny-all policy 

apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all
  namespace: anihpj
spec: {}

B.10 AuthorizationPolicy — Allow Rules

yaml — allow ingress → jobpost + jobpost → users 

# Allow ingress → jobpost-api (GET/POST)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-ingress-to-jobpost
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: jobpost-api
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals:
        - "cluster.local/ns/istio-system/sa/istio-ingressgateway"
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET", "POST"]
---
# Allow jobpost-api → user-service (GET only)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-jobpost-to-users
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: user-service
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals:
        - "cluster.local/ns/anihpj/sa/jobpost-api"
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET"]
        paths: ["/api/users/*"]

B.11 ServiceEntry — External Payment API

yaml — ServiceEntry for Stripe 

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata:
  name: stripe-payments
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  hosts:
  - api.stripe.com
  ports:
  - number: 443
    name: https
    protocol: HTTPS
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL
  resolution: DNS

B.12 RequestAuthentication — JWT Validation

yaml — JWT validation for API endpoints 

apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: RequestAuthentication
metadata:
  name: jwt-auth
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  jwtRules:
  - issuer: "auth-service.anihpj.svc.cluster.local"
    jwksUri: "http://auth-service/.well-known/jwks.json"

B.13 Telemetry — Custom Sampling + Metrics Labels

yaml — Telemetry resource 

apiVersion: telemetry.istio.io/v1alpha1
kind: Telemetry
metadata:
  name: anihpj-telemetry
  namespace: anihpj
spec:
  tracing:
  - randomSamplingPercentage: 1.0
  metrics:
  - providers:
    - name: prometheus
    overrides:
    - match:
        metric: REQUEST_COUNT
      tagOverrides:
        job_category:
          value: request.headers["x-job-category"]

📎 Appendix C: istioctl Command Reference

📥 INSTALLATION & SETUP

CommandPurpose
istioctl install --set profile=demo -yInstall Istio with demo profile (all tools)
istioctl install -f custom-iop.yamlInstall using custom IstioOperator config
istioctl verify-installVerify installation is correct
istioctl upgradeIn-place upgrade (use canary for production!)
istioctl uninstall --purgeRemove all Istio resources
istioctl profile listList available installation profiles

🔍 DEBUGGING & DIAGNOSTICS

CommandPurpose
istioctl proxy-statusCheck sync status of ALL proxies (SYNCED/STALE)
istioctl proxy-config cluster <pod> -n <ns>Show upstream clusters Envoy knows about
istioctl proxy-config route <pod> -n <ns>Show routing rules applied to this proxy
istioctl proxy-config listener <pod> -n <ns>Show listeners (ports) on this proxy
istioctl proxy-config endpoint <pod> -n <ns>Show endpoint discovery (which pods exist)
istioctl proxy-config secret <pod> -n <ns>Show SPIFFE certificates in Envoy
istioctl analyze -n <ns>Validate config — catches 80% of errors!
istioctl analyze --all-namespacesValidate config across entire cluster
istioctl authn tls-check <pod> -n <ns>Check mTLS configuration for a pod
istioctl bug-reportGenerate diagnostic bundle for support

🖥️ DASHBOARDS

CommandPurpose
istioctl dashboard kialiOpen Kiali — service graph, config validation
istioctl dashboard grafanaOpen Grafana — RED dashboards
istioctl dashboard jaegerOpen Jaeger — distributed traces
istioctl dashboard prometheusOpen Prometheus — raw metrics query
istioctl dashboard zipkinOpen Zipkin — alternative tracing backend
istioctl dashboard envoy <pod> -n <ns>Open Envoy admin UI for a specific proxy
💡 ICA Exam Tip

The 3 most important istioctl commands for the exam: istioctl analyze -n <ns> (validate config), istioctl proxy-status (check sync), istioctl proxy-config cluster <pod> -n <ns> (inspect Envoy). Know these by heart.

📎 Appendix D: Common Istio Errors & Solutions

Error / SymptomLikely CauseFix
Pod shows 1/1 not 2/2Sidecar not injectedLabel ns: istio-injection=enabled
503 RBAC: access deniedAuthorizationPolicy blockingAdd explicit ALLOW policy
503 upstream connect errorDR mTLS mode mismatchMatch PeerAuthentication mode
VS not routingSubset not in DestinationRuleAdd matching subset to DR
Traffic to all podsMissing version labelAdd version label to Deployment
analyze: "host not found"Service name mismatch in VSMatch VS host to K8s svc name
High latency after installTracing 100% sampling overheadSet sampling to 1% in Telemetry
Circuit breaker trips oftenoutlierDetection too aggressiveIncrease consecutiveGatewayErrors
External APIs failingREGISTRY_ONLY mode activeAdd ServiceEntry for external host
PROXY_STATUS: STALENetwork issue to istiodCheck istiod pod health, port 15012

📎 Appendix E: Istio Terminology Glossary

TermDefinition
Ambient MeshSidecar-free Istio mode using ztunnel (L4) + waypoint proxies (L7)
AuthorizationPolicyIstio CRD for access control — defines WHO can call WHAT
Circuit BreakerPattern: stop sending requests to a failing service to prevent cascading failures
Control Planeistiod — manages configuration, certificates, and policies for all proxies
CRDCustom Resource Definition — extends Kubernetes API with Istio resources
Data PlaneAll Envoy sidecar proxies that handle actual service-to-service traffic
DestinationRuleDefines policies for traffic going TO a service: LB, subsets, circuit breaker, mTLS
EnvoyHigh-performance L7 proxy; Istio's sidecar proxy handling all mesh traffic
Fault InjectionDeliberately inject delays/errors to test system resilience
Gateway (Istio)Entry/exit point to the mesh for external traffic (ingress + egress)
istiodIstio control plane daemon (Pilot + Citadel + Galley combined)
istioctlIstio CLI tool — like kubectl but for Istio operations
JaegerDistributed tracing backend; visualizes request traces as Gantt charts
KialiIstio mesh visualization console — service graph, validation, YAML wizards
mTLSMutual TLS — both client and server verify each other's certificates
Outlier DetectionDestinationRule setting that implements circuit breaking by ejecting failing hosts
PeerAuthenticationIstio CRD that configures mTLS mode (PERMISSIVE/STRICT/DISABLE)
Pilotistiod component: reads CRDs, translates to Envoy config via xDS API
RED MetricsRate, Errors, Duration — Istio auto-collects these from every Envoy proxy
RequestAuthenticationIstio CRD for JWT token validation at the mesh level
Service MeshInfrastructure layer that manages service-to-service communication
ServiceEntryIstio CRD to register external services (Stripe, SendGrid, S3) in the mesh
Sidecar (container)Envoy proxy container injected alongside your application container
SPIFFESecure Production Identity Framework — certificate standard used by Istio
SVIDSPIFFE Verifiable Identity Document — workload X.509 certificate
TelemetryIstio CRD for configuring metrics, tracing, and logging collection
VirtualServiceIstio CRD defining routing rules: URI match, weight split, retries, timeouts
Waypoint ProxyAmbient mesh L7 proxy per namespace (optional, replaces sidecar L7 features)
xDS APIProtocol used by istiod to dynamically configure all Envoy proxies
ztunnelAmbient mesh L4 proxy per Node; handles mTLS without per-pod sidecars

📎 Appendix G: Local Dev Quick Start

bash — From zero to Istio mesh in 10 commands 

# 1. Start minikube (4 CPUs, 8GB RAM, 40GB disk)
minikube start --cpus=4 --memory=8192 --disk-size=40g

# 2. Install Istio (demo profile = all tools)
curl -L https://istio.io/downloadIstio | sh -
cd istio-1.22.*
export PATH=$PWD/bin:$PATH
istioctl install --set profile=demo -y

# 3. Verify installation (7 pods running)
kubectl get pods -n istio-system

# 4. Create and label anihpj namespace
kubectl create namespace anihpj
kubectl label namespace anihpj istio-injection=enabled

# 5. Deploy anihpj
kubectl apply -f anihpj/k8s/ -n anihpj

# 6. Verify sidecars (all pods should show 2/2)
kubectl get pods -n anihpj

# 7. Check proxy sync (all should be SYNCED)
istioctl proxy-status

# 8. Validate config (0 errors expected)
istioctl analyze -n anihpj

# 9. Open dashboards
istioctl dashboard kiali
istioctl dashboard grafana
istioctl dashboard jaeger

# 10. Test traffic
kubectl exec -it deploy/jobpost-api -n anihpj -- \
  curl -s user-service/users/

📎 Appendix H: Quick-Reference Cheat Sheet

🧭 ISTIO CRD SELECTION GUIDE

I want to...Use this Istio resource
Accept external HTTPS trafficGateway
Route by URL pathVirtualService (http.match.uri)
Do a canary deploymentVirtualService (weight) + DestinationRule (subsets)
Add retry logic / timeoutVirtualService (retries / timeout)
Inject faults for testingVirtualService (fault)
Load balance / circuit breakerDestinationRule (loadBalancer / outlierDetection)
Encrypt service-to-servicePeerAuthentication (STRICT)
Block a service from callingAuthorizationPolicy (DENY)
Validate JWT tokensRequestAuthentication
Call an external APIServiceEntry
Add non-K8s workloads to meshWorkloadEntry
See service topology / traces / metricsKiali / Jaeger / Grafana
🔑
mTLS Modes

PERMISSIVE — allow both HTTP + mTLS (migration)
STRICT — mTLS only
DISABLE — no TLS

⚖️
Canary Pattern

1. Deploy v2 (replicas: 2)
2. VS weight: v1=95%, v2=5%
3. Monitor Kiali/Grafana
4. Ramp: 10→25→50→100%
Rollback: set v2=0% instantly

📊
RED Metrics (auto)

R = Rate (req/s)
E = Errors (% 4xx/5xx)
D = Duration (p50/p95/p99)
Zero code changes!

🔌
Circuit Breaker

outlierDetection:
  consecutiveGatewayErrors: 5
  interval: 30s
  baseEjectionTime: 30s
